topic.title: Typography and Element Showcase
topic.shortdesc: A comprehensive demonstration of every DITA element supported by the dita2epub plugin, with examples of the rendered output.

body.p: This chapter serves as a visual and structural test for every content element the plugin transforms. If you are reading a well-formatted EPUB, each section below should render with the appropriate styling, semantic markup, and accessibility attributes.

section.title: Paragraphs and Drop Caps
section.p: The first paragraph of a chapter can optionally display a decorative drop capsdrop cap when the epub.drop.caps parameter is set to yes. Drop caps are automatically suppressed for CJK languages (Japanese, Chinese, Korean) where they are typographically inappropriate.

Subsequent paragraphs render normally. The default stylesheet uses a system font stack with 16px base size, 1.6 line-height, and orphan/widow control to prevent single lines from appearing alone at the top or bottom of a page.

section.title: Inline Formatting
section.p: The plugin supports the standard DITA inline elements: bold text renders as <strong>, italic text renders as <em>, and code phrases render as <code> with a light gray background and monospace font.

Inline quotations use the <q> element. With the default settings, they render using the browser's built-in quotation marks: like this. When epub.locale.quotes=yes, the plugin substitutes locale-aware quotation marks — for example, French guillemets or German Anführungszeichen.

section.title: Footnotes
section.p: footnotesFootnotes are a critical feature for academic and professional publishing. This paragraph contains a footnoteThis is the first footnote in the typography showcase. Note that it appears as a superscript number in the text, with the full note collected at the end of the topic in an endnotes section. to demonstrate inline reference markers. Here is a secondSecond footnotes demonstrate sequential numbering. Each footnote includes a backlink (the ↩ symbol) that returns the reader to the reference point in the text. for testing sequential numbering.

A third footnoteThis footnote appears in a separate paragraph to verify that numbering continues correctly across paragraph boundaries within the same topic. later in the text verifies that numbering continues correctly across the entire topic.

section.title: Figures and Images
section.p: Figures wrap images in a semantic <figure> element with a <figcaption>. When epub.figure.numbering=global, each figure receives an auto-generated label (Figure 1., Figure 2., etc.) in the reader's language:

fig.title: The DITA to EPUB Transformation Pipeline

image.alt: Workflow diagram showing DITA source files passing through XSLT transformation to produce EPUB 3 output including XHTML, OPF, and navigation documents

section.p: The figure above uses an SVG image, which renders crisply at any zoom level. The plugin also supports PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP formats.

section.title: Tables
section.p: tablesrenderingTables demonstrate several features: header row styling, column alignment, zebra striping, and column/row spanning.

section.title: Blockquotes
section.p: The DITA <lq> element renders as a styled blockquote with an optional source attribution:
section.lq: Digital publishing transforms how we create, distribute, and consume written content. The transition to standards-based formats ensures long-term preservation and universal accessibility.
section.p: The @reftitle attribute provides a human-readable label for the source link.

section.title: Did You Know?
section.p: EPUB 3.3EPUB 3.3 became a W3C Recommendation on 25 May 2023, making it the first version of the EPUB specification published under W3C governance. This milestone ensures the format's continued evolution under the same organization that maintains HTML, CSS, and other core web standards.

section.title: Notes and Admonitions
section.p: The plugin renders all six DITA note typesnote types with distinct visual styling and localized labels:
section.note: A generic note provides supplementary information that may be useful but is not essential.
A tip note offers a shortcut, best practice, or time-saving suggestion.
An important note highlights critical information that the reader should not overlook.
A warning note alerts the reader to a potential problem or common mistake that could cause incorrect results.
A caution note indicates a risk of data loss, performance degradation, or other negative consequences if the advice is not followed.
A danger note signals a severe risk. In technical documentation, this typically means irreversible data loss, security vulnerabilities, or system instability.

section.title: Definition Lists
section.p: Definition lists are useful for glossary-style content within a topic:

dlentry.dd: Content that adapts to the reader's screen size, font preferences, and accessibility settings. This is the default and recommended EPUB content model.
Content with a fixed page size and position, similar to PDF. Not supported by this plugin.
The ordered list of content documents in an EPUB, defining the default reading order from cover to index.
